rawFindings.title: Incorrect image URL resolution when image path is relative
rawFindings.explanation: The patch changes the image URL resolution logic to manually prepend a leading slash if missing, then directly concatenate config.url and path, instead of using url.resolve. This can produce incorrect URLs if config.url contains a pathname or a trailing slash, or if path includes query parameters. The previous method using url.resolve handled these cases properly, ensuring correct absolute URLs.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to the original approach using urlFn.resolve(url || config.url, path) to correctly resolve image URLs, preserving handling of subdirectories and relative paths.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect URL resolution for relative image paths
rawFindings.explanation: The original code uses url.resolve to correctly resolve both absolute and relative image paths based on the page URL or site URL. The new code replaces this with a simple string concatenation that only prepends a slash if the path does not start with '/'. This change breaks cases where the site is hosted in a subdirectory or when the path is relative, leading to incorrect image URLs in the generated open graph tags.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using url.resolve(url || config.url, path) to resolve image paths correctly, ensuring proper handling of relative and absolute paths, and subdirectory hosting.
